title: Smooth-Projective Serre Duality and Flag-Variety Line Bundles

items.title: Dualizing line bundle and trace datum of a smooth projective variety
items.statement: Assume AC. For a smooth projective pure n-dimensional scheme X over a field k, define ω_X=det Ω¹_{X/k}. A normalized Serre trace is a k-linear map t_X:H^n(X,ω_X)→k agreeing with the Laurent-coefficient residue trace on projective space and compatible with regular-immersion adjunction. Its existence, nondegeneracy and embedding independence are claims of the later smooth-projective theorem, not part of this definition.

references.title: Ravi Vakil, Foundations of Algebraic Geometry Classes 53–54
references.locator: Class 53 §§1–5 and Class 54 §§7, 11; omitted connecting-morphism proof is a local obligation

items.strategy: Use the finite locally free differential sheaf to form its determinant. Type the trace datum using the AC-qualified sheaf-cohomology construction, and fix its projective-space residue normalization. Do not use a general trace in proving its existence; AC is inherited through the sheaf-cohomology and smoothness suppliers.

items.title: Top-cohomology residue pairing on projective space
items.statement: Assume AC. For n≥1 and every d≥0, multiplication followed by the Laurent coefficient of (x_0⋯x_n)^−1 is a perfect pairing H⁰(P^n_k,O(d))×H^n(P^n_k,O(−n−1−d))→k, compatible with multiplication by homogeneous polynomials. For n=0 it is ordinary multiplication k×k→k under O(d)≅O.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Cohomology of Schemes, §§30.2, 30.8, 30.14
Ravi Vakil, Foundations of Algebraic Geometry Classes 53 and 54

items.strategy: Use the batch-9 exact monomial bases, pairing x^a with x^(−a−1). Every degree-d basis element has exactly one dual top-cohomology basis monomial. Check naturality under multiplication directly on monomials and handle P⁰ separately; AC enters through the supplied cohomology/cup construction.

items.title: Serre duality for projective-space twists
items.statement: Assume AC. With ω_{P^n}=O(−n−1) and residue trace, for every integer d and q the cup/evaluation pairing H^q(P^n,O(d))×H^{n−q}(P^n,O(−d−n−1))→k is perfect.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Cohomology of Schemes, §§30.2, 30.8, 30.14
The Stacks Project, Duality for Schemes, §27
Ravi Vakil, Foundations of Algebraic Geometry Classes 53 and 54

items.strategy: Compute det Ω_{P^n/k}=O(−n−1) from the standard coordinate transition Jacobian. The batch-9 cohomology theorem gives zero in intermediate degrees; in degrees 0 and n the preceding Laurent residue pairs complementary monomial bases. For P⁰ use ordinary multiplication. The trace is the chosen residue coefficient; AC is inherited from cohomology.

items.title: Finite twisted locally free resolutions on projective space
items.statement: Assume AC. For a field k and n≥0, every coherent O_{P^n_k}-module F has a finite exact resolution by finite direct sums of O(d), of length at most n+1 after sheafifying a finitely generated graded polynomial-module presentation.

references.title: Ravi Vakil, Foundations of Algebraic Geometry Classes 53–54
references.locator: Class 53 §§1–5 and Class 54 §§7, 11; omitted connecting-morphism proof is a local obligation

items.strategy: First use the in-run section-extension lemma on every D_+(x_i) to identify F with the associated sheaf of its graded global-section tail: local sections become global after an x_i-power, and the tail is finite by the batch-9 graded-section theorem. Take a finitely generated graded S=k[x_0,…,x_n]-module M whose associated sheaf is F from the batch-9 graded section tail; sheafification ignores finite irrelevant torsion. Repeated homogeneous finite free covers have finite graded kernels since S is Noetherian. At m=(x_0,…,x_n), regularity and the published Auslander–Buchsbaum–Serre bound make the (n+1)st syzygy K_m free. Lift a homogeneous basis of K/mK to a graded free cover Q→K. Graded Nakayama makes it surjective; Q_m→K_m is an isomorphism by minimal rank, so its graded kernel localizes to zero at m and must itself be zero, as any nonzero finite graded module has a homogeneous element surviving m-localization. Sheafify, using exact localization and ~S(d)=O(d). AC is inherited from the graded-cohomology and regular-local suppliers.

items.title: Injective modules are flasque and Ext from the structure sheaf is cohomology
items.statement: Assume AC. For a ringed space (Y,O_Y): every injective O_Y-module is flasque as an abelian sheaf, and for every O_Y-module G and q\u22650 there is a canonical isomorphism Ext^q_{O_Y}(O_Y,G) \u2245 H^q(Y,G), natural in G, whose degree-zero case is evaluation at the unit section.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Sheaves of Modules
references.locator: Lemma 19.5.1 (tag 01DI), enough injectives for sheaves of modules on a ringed space

references.title: The Stacks Project, Cohomology of Sheaves

items.strategy: Construct extension by zero for O-modules and use it to show restriction maps out of an injective module split; conclude that O-injective modules are flasque abelian sheaves, hence acyclic for global sections, and compare the acyclic-resolution isomorphism with Hom(O_Y,-) = global sections on the supplied functorial injective resolution.

items.title: Sheaf Ext of coherent modules
items.statement: Assume AC. On a ringed space (Y,O_Y), for O_Y-modules F,G choose an O_Y-injective resolution G→I•. Define global Ext^q_Y(F,G)=H^q Hom_{O_Y}(F,I•) and sheaf Ext^q_Y(F,G)=H^q of the internal Hom complex. O-module injective comparison maps and homotopies make these independent of the supplied resolution. Local free resolutions compute sheaf Ext when available, but not global Ext directly.

references.title: Ravi Vakil, Foundations of Algebraic Geometry Classes 53–54
references.locator: Class 53 §§1–5 and Class 54 §§7, 11; omitted connecting-morphism proof is a local obligation

items.strategy: Use the in-run O-module enough-injectives theorem, not abstract enough-projectives or injectives only in abelian sheaves. Apply O-linear Hom and internal Hom to supplied comparison homotopies; a chain homotopy remains one after internal Hom. AC supplies the injective resolution and comparison choices.

items.title: Long exact global sheaf Ext sequence in the first variable
items.statement: Assume AC. On a ringed space (Y,O_Y) with commutative structure sheaf, a short exact sequence 0→F′→F→F″→0 of O_Y-modules and an O_Y-module G induce a natural long exact sequence 0→Hom(F″,G)→Hom(F,G)→Hom(F′,G)→Ext¹_Y(F″,G)→Ext¹_Y(F,G)→⋯, using the injective-resolution global Ext construction.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Duality for Schemes, §27
Ravi Vakil, Foundations of Algebraic Geometry Classes 53 and 54

items.strategy: Fix one O_Y-injective resolution G→I•. For each p, injectivity of I^p makes 0→Hom(F″,I^p)→Hom(F,I^p)→Hom(F′,I^p)→0 exact. Take cohomology to obtain the long exact sequence; H⁰ is ordinary Hom, and naturality under resolution comparison follows from homotopy invariance. AC supplies the O-module resolution.

items.title: Serre duality for coherent sheaves on projective space
items.statement: Assume AC. For every coherent F on P^n_k, the natural pairing Ext^{n−q}_{P^n}(F,ω_{P^n})×H^q(P^n,F)→k is perfect for 0≤q≤n.

references.title: Ravi Vakil, Foundations of Algebraic Geometry Classes 53–54
references.locator: Class 53 §§1–5 and Class 54 §§7, 11; omitted connecting-morphism proof is a local obligation

items.strategy: Define Ext^{n−q}(F,ω)×H^q(F)→H^n(ω)→k by Yoneda composition and residue. It is perfect for sums of twists by the preceding twist theorem. For each short exact 0→K→P→F→0 from the finite twist resolution, compare the global Ext first-variable long exact sequence with the k-linear dual of the cohomology long exact sequence. Prove connecting-square compatibility by the chain-level Yoneda product on an injective resolution (including the sign from the boundary); then use the five lemma and induction on resolution length. Finite-dimensionality from the in-run projective cohomology theorem licenses dualizing exact sequences. AC supplies O-module injectives and cohomology.

items.title: Smooth closed immersion is regular with exact conormal sequence
items.statement: Assume AC. If i:X↪P^N_k is a closed immersion with X smooth of pure codimension c, then I/I² is locally free of rank c, its local generators form a regular sequence, and 0→I/I²→i*Ω¹_{P^N/k}→Ω¹_{X/k}→0 is exact.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Duality for Schemes, §27
Ravi Vakil, Foundations of Algebraic Geometry Classes 53 and 54

items.strategy: At every scheme point x, the affine finite-type local-dimension formula and smooth pure dimensions give dim O_{P^N,x}-dim O_{X,x}=N-n=c, even when x is not closed. The regular-local/regular-quotient criterion supplies a length-c regular parameter sequence generating the ideal. Koszul H1 makes its classes a free basis of I/I². The smooth differential modules have ranks N and n; the right-exact conormal sequence surjects from a free rank-c module onto the rank-c kernel of a split surjection, hence is short exact. This avoids treating arbitrary regular parameters as a basis of relative differentials over imperfect fields.

items.title: Adjunction for a smooth closed subvariety
items.statement: Assume AC. For a smooth closed immersion i:X↪P^N_k with ideal I and normal bundle N=(I/I²)∨, ω_X≅i*ω_{P^N}⊗det N.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Duality for Schemes, §27
Ravi Vakil, Foundations of Algebraic Geometry Classes 53 and 54

items.strategy: Take determinants of the short exact conormal sequence: det Ω_X = i*det Ω_P ⊗ det(I/I²)^∨. Use the projective Jacobian calculation for det Ω_P and identify det(I/I²)^∨ with det N. Check the local determinant transition is canonical; AC is inherited through the conormal supplier.

items.title: Koszul sheaf Ext of a smooth regular immersion
items.statement: Assume AC. For i:X↪P^N_k smooth of codimension c and E finite locally free on X, the sheaf Ext^q_{P^N}(i_*E,ω_{P^N}) vanishes for q≠c and equals i_*(E∨⊗ω_X) for q=c.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Duality for Schemes, §27
Ravi Vakil, Foundations of Algebraic Geometry Classes 53 and 54

items.strategy: On a neighborhood where I=(f_1,…,f_c) is a regular sequence and E is free over O_X, lift a basis and use the Koszul resolution of i_*E. Dualizing it against ω_P gives cohomology only in degree c, identified locally with i_*(E∨⊗det(I/I²)^∨⊗i*ω_P). Check changes of regular sequence act by the inverse determinant and changes of E frame by the dual transition, so these local identifications glue to i_*(E∨⊗ω_X) using adjunction. AC is inherited through O-module Ext and conormal inputs.

items.title: Local-to-global Ext collapse for a regular immersion
items.statement: Assume AC. Under the preceding regular-immersion hypotheses, Ext^{c+j}_{P^N}(i_*E,ω_{P^N})≅H^j(X,E∨⊗ω_X), naturally in E.
items.strategy: Apply the published Grothendieck spectral sequence to internal Hom(i_*E,−) followed by Γ(P^N,−). An O-injective I makes internal Hom(i_*E,I) flasque: for U⊂V extend a local map along the stalkwise monomorphism j_!(i_*E|U)→i_*E|V, using exact extension-by-zero and injectivity of I|V. Thus internal Hom sends injectives to Γ-acyclics. The spectral sequence has E₂^{p,q}=H^p(P^N,sheaf Ext^q(i_*E,ω_P)) and abuts to global Ext^{p+q}. The Koszul lemma concentrates at q=c, so its edge gives the claimed isomorphism; exact closed-immersion pushforward preserves cohomology and identifies H^p(P^N,i_*M)=H^p(X,M). Check naturality in E. AC supplies injective comparison data.

items.title: Rational-point Koszul residue normalization for a smooth projective embedding
items.statement: Assume AC. Let i:X↪P^N_k be a smooth closed projective immersion of pure dimension n and let x∈X(k). For regular parameters t_1,…,t_n at x, the local Koszul class in Ext^n_X(k_x,ω_X) normalized by dt_1∧⋯∧dt_n maps, under the conormal adjunction and Yoneda composition for x↪X↪P^N, to the ambient point class in Ext^N_{P^N}(k_x,ω_{P^N}); evaluation at 1∈H⁰(k_x) followed by the normalized projective Laurent trace sends this class to 1. The normalization is independent of parameter and ambient coordinate choices and commutes with field extension.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Duality for Schemes, Lemmas 15.4–15.5
references.locator: §15, Lemmas 15.4–15.5, Koszul Ext multiplication and determinant signs

references.title: Ravi Vakil, Foundations of Algebraic Geometry Classes 53–54

items.strategy: Move the rational point by a projective linear change of coordinates to [1:0:⋯:0], and write z_a=x_a/x_0 on its affine chart. The Koszul resolution of the point by x_1,…,x_N, paired with the Euler trivialization of ω_P, sends its top Ext generator through the Čech–Koszul connecting map to the class (x_0⋯x_N)^−1 on the standard projective cover; its Laurent coefficient is 1. Check this connecting map on the double complex, including the ordered Koszul differential sign. Near x choose normal equations f_1,…,f_c for X and parameters t_1,…,t_n on X, lifting the latter to P, so (f,t) is a regular parameter sequence at x. The tensor product K(f)⊗K(t) is K(f,t); the Stacks Koszul exterior/Yoneda calculation identifies its top class with the composition of the two immersion classes. Use the same order f then t in det(I/I²)^∨⊗ω_P≅ω_X, so the shuffle sign and determinant orientation agree. Under any change from (f,t) to z, the top Koszul class transforms by the inverse Jacobian determinant and the top differential form by the determinant; their product is invariant. This reduces the composite residue to the standard-coordinate coefficient 1. The formulas are polynomial over k and therefore commute with field extension; n=0 and c=0 use the empty Koszul complex. AC is inherited through the Ext and cohomology suppliers.

items.title: Embedding compatibility of smooth-projective Gysin traces
items.statement: Assume AC. For two closed projective embeddings i:X↪P^N_k and j:X↪P^M_k of a smooth projective pure n-dimensional X, the scalar maps H^n(X,ω_X)→k obtained from the local Koszul-Ext collapse, projective-space coherent duality, evaluation at 1∈H⁰(X,O_X), and the normalized Laurent traces agree; the comparison is compatible with finite locally free bundle maps on X, isomorphisms of embedded data, and field extension.
items.strategy: For each embedding, projective-space coherent duality, the regular-immersion Ext collapse and adjunction give perfect cup pairings for locally free sheaves with the induced trace t_i:H^n(X,ω_X)→k. Extend the top-degree pairing functorially to each coherent F by a two-term presentation from sufficiently twisted globally generated sheaves: Hom_X(F,ω_X)≅H^n(X,F)^∨ (Vakil Class 53, Proposition 2.1). Yoneda then compares the two trace pairs by a unique automorphism of ω_X, necessarily multiplication by a global unit u (Vakil Proposition 2.2). Base-change the entire construction and both traces to an algebraic closure using flat coherent-cohomology base change, smooth differential base change, and the coefficient-defined projective Laurent trace; faithful flatness will descend equality. Over the algebraic closure, test the two top-degree coherent pairings on every rational closed-point sheaf k_x. By Yoneda naturality, their discrepancy is multiplication by u(x). The rational-point Koszul residue-normalization lemma evaluates each embedding's pairing on the same intrinsic Ext^n_X(k_x,ω_X) class at 1∈H⁰(k_x) as 1, so u(x)=1 for every closed x. Smooth X is reduced and finite type over an algebraically closed field; on affine opens the Jacobson closed-point radical criterion gives u−1=0. Hence u=1, both traces agree, and equality descends to k. The same Yoneda cup/evaluation naturality gives compatibility for every finite locally free E. Check all connecting maps and Koszul signs in the point-normalization lemma; do not replace them with a bare citation to general duality. AC is inherited through Ext and cohomology.

references.title: Ravi Vakil, Foundations of Algebraic Geometry Classes 53–54
references.locator: Class 53 §§1–5 and Class 54 §§7, 11; omitted connecting-morphism proof is a local obligation

items.title: Serre duality for locally free sheaves on a smooth projective variety
items.statement: Assume AC. For a smooth projective pure n-dimensional k-scheme X and finite locally free E, there is a normalized trace t_X:H^n(X,ω_X)→k making H^q(X,E)×H^{n−q}(X,E∨⊗ω_X)→k a functorial perfect pairing for all q.

references.title: Ravi Vakil, Foundations of Algebraic Geometry Classes 53–54
references.locator: Class 53 §§1–5 and Class 54 §§7, 11; omitted connecting-morphism proof is a local obligation

items.strategy: For a chosen projective embedding i:X↪P^N, combine projective coherent Ext duality for i_*E with the regular-immersion Ext collapse and determinant adjunction to obtain a perfect pairing. Identify its Yoneda evaluation with cup/evaluation H^q(E)×H^{n−q}(E∨⊗ω_X) and define the trace via E=O_X and the unit section. The preceding Gysin compatibility must prove the resulting trace is independent of embedding and functorial; componentwise normalization handles disconnected X and n=0. AC enters through the cited Ext/cohomology suppliers.

items.title: Complex semisimple algebraic group, Borel, and flag variety
items.statement: Assume AC. Fix a connected simply connected complex semisimple affine algebraic group G, maximal torus T with Lie algebra h, a positive root system Φ⁺ and simple roots Δ; write B for the connected algebraic subgroup with Lie algebra b=h⊕n⁺, U for its unipotent radical, W=N_G(T)/T, and X=G/B for the algebraic quotient constructed below. A minimal parabolic P_α contains B and the negative simple-root subgroup U_{−α}; this P_α is not the maximal-parabolic convention.
items.strategy: Fix the Lie root conventions from published suppliers and the group/quotient notation only; the later root-factorization and projective-orbit lemmas establish B, P_α and G/B rather than assuming that a smooth Lie quotient is an algebraic one. AC is inherited from the published root theory.

items.title: A finite-type affine algebraic group has a faithful rational representation
items.statement: Every finite-type affine group scheme G over C admits a finite-dimensional rational representation ρ:G→GL(V) that is a closed immersion.

references.title: J. S. Milne, Algebraic Groups (2022)
references.locator: §4(c) Proposition 4.7, Corollary 4.8, §4(d) Theorem 4.9 and Corollary 4.10; printed pp.86–87

items.strategy: Put A=O(G), a finitely generated Hopf algebra, and use right translation to make A a rational G-comodule. For a∈A, write Δ(a)=∑a_i⊗b_i with the b_i linearly independent; coassociativity and coefficient comparison show the span of a and the finitely many a_i lies in a finite-dimensional subcomodule. Choose finitely many algebra generators of A and sum their finite-dimensional subcomodules to obtain a finite-dimensional stable V⊂A containing those generators. In a basis e_j of V, write Δ(e_j)=∑e_i⊗a_ij. Applying the counit to the first factor expresses every e_j as a linear combination of the matrix coefficients a_ij, so the induced Hopf map O(GL(V))→A is surjective. Its dual ρ:G→GL(V) is therefore a closed immersion, in particular faithful over every test algebra. Only finite selections occur; this lemma itself is choice-free even though its later root-theoretic consumers assume AC.

items.title: Algebraic root subgroups from root exponentials
items.statement: Assume AC. For each root α of (G,T), a nonzero root vector e_α integrates to a closed T-normalized algebraic subgroup U_α≅G_a with Lie algebra g_α and conjugation t u_α(z)t^−1=u_α(α(t)z); the opposite root vectors form an sl₂-triple.
items.strategy: Use the preceding finite-dimensional faithful rational representation to embed G as a closed subgroup of GL(V). The published sl₂ theory makes the matrix of e_α nilpotent on V, so exp(z e_α) is a finite polynomial matrix. Apply published naturality of Lie-group exponentials to the inclusion G(C)→GL(V) for each complex tangent vector z e_α: the matrix exponential is the image of exp_G(z e_α), hence lies in G(C). Every polynomial defining G therefore vanishes identically on that polynomial curve, making it an algebraic Ga subgroup. The polynomial logarithm in the upper-unitriangular realization identifies its image as closed and the map as an isomorphism. Torus conjugation follows by differentiating, and the opposite triple is the published root-sl₂ result. AC implies the countable-choice exponential supplier and is also inherited from the root theorem.

items.title: Rank-one SL₂ homomorphism and Weyl representative
items.statement: Assume AC. For each root α there is an algebraic homomorphism φ_α:SL₂(C)→G with central kernel contained in {±I}, mapping the two unipotent root subgroups isomorphically to U_{±α}, the diagonal torus to the coroot α∨(C×), and the standard Weyl matrix to a representative n_α of s_α in N_G(T).
items.strategy: Use the published matrix polar decomposition g=UH for g∈SL₂(C): det H=|det g|=1 and det U=1, so g↦UH^t deformation retracts SL₂(C) onto SU₂. The explicit matrices [[a,b],[-conj(b),conj(a)]] identify SU₂ with S³, which is simply connected by the published sphere theorem. Apply the published Lie second fundamental theorem to the sl₂-triple, viewing SL₂(C) and G(C) as real Lie groups; AC implies its countable-choice hypothesis. The integrated map is holomorphic because its differential commutes with complex structures at the identity and translations transport this condition everywhere. Its restrictions to the two additive subgroups are the polynomial root exponentials; the diagonal restriction is algebraic because every eigenvalue of the sl₂ Cartan element in the faithful finite-dimensional representation is integral, giving t↦t^m. The two Gauss charts cover SL₂ and express the integrated map by those regular restrictions, so it is algebraic. Its differential is injective, hence the kernel is finite central, therefore contained in {±I}; calculate the Weyl matrix conjugation on the torus. AC enters via Lie integration and published sl₂ representation/root structure.

items.title: Borel, opposite unipotent groups and root coordinates
items.statement: Assume AC. The root exponentials for positive roots form a closed connected unipotent subgroup U with polynomial product coordinates ∏_{α∈Φ⁺}U_α≅U in any height-compatible order; B=T⋉U is a maximal connected solvable algebraic subgroup with Lie algebra b, an opposite B⁻=T⋉U⁻ exists, and X*(B)≅X*(T).
items.strategy: Use a faithful weight basis in which positive root matrices are strictly upper triangular. Polynomial exp/log identify the nilpotent Lie algebra n⁺ with a closed unipotent subgroup; triangular BCH by root height gives a polynomial inverse to the ordered product of root exponentials. Repeat for n⁻. T normalizes U and intersects it trivially, giving B=T⋉U. Any solvable Lie subalgebra containing b and a negative-root component is ad(h)-stable and contains a negative root vector; with its positive partner it contains an sl₂, contradiction, so b is maximal solvable and B is Borel. A regular character of each Ga factor is trivial, hence restriction X*(B)→X*(T) is bijective. AC is inherited from Lie-root structure.

items.title: The opposite-root big cell is an open chart
items.statement: Assume AC. Multiplication U⁻×T×U→G is an open immersion with dense image Ω=U⁻B; its quotient chart Ω/B is U⁻≅A^{|Φ⁺|}.
items.strategy: The Lie algebra sum n⁻⊕h⊕n⁺=g makes the multiplication map étale at the identity; translate and use the triangular adjoint action of U to keep its differential invertible everywhere. Uniqueness of opposite/positive root factorization holds functorially over every test algebra by the triangular root coordinates, so the map is a monomorphism. The in-run étale-openness theorem makes its image Ω open; over Ω the map is a surjective flat monomorphism of finite presentation. Prove this is an isomorphism locally by the faithfully-flat equalizer A→B⇉B⊗_A B on affine charts: monomorphism makes the two arrows equal, and faithful flatness makes A their equalizer. Glue the inverse, proving an open immersion without treating a cited scheme theorem as an unproved step. G is connected and hence irreducible as a smooth algebraic group, making Ω dense. Its B quotient has the displayed root coordinates and a section u↦u. AC is inherited from root-factorization and étale openness.

items.title: Bruhat double cosets from rank-one multiplication
items.statement: Assume AC. The normalizer quotient N_G(T)/T is the finite constant Weyl group W(Φ), and G is the disjoint union of Bn_wB. Each cell is U_w×B with U_w≅A^{ℓ(w)}.
items.strategy: Prove positive-chamber normalizer elements lie in T using root-exponential naturality and the open big cell; chamber simple transitivity identifies N_G(T)/T with W(Φ). Show the closed normalizer is smooth and its finite T-cosets give the fppf quotient. Derive the two-cell multiplication from the explicit SL₂ matrix identity and the minimal-parabolic two-cell supplier. Root-group generation and the open big cell give coverage. A height-triangular root-coordinate change gives U=U_w U^w; restriction of the big-cell isomorphism supplies each cell chart. Unique T-fixed points in the charts give disjointness, and the inversion-number supplier gives dimension.

items.title: Minimal parabolic from one negative simple root
items.statement: Assume AC. For α∈Δ, the subgroup P_α generated by B and U_{−α} is a closed connected algebraic subgroup with P_α=B⊔Bn_αB, Lie(P_α)=b⊕g_{−α}, and P_α/B has the two affine charts of P¹.
items.strategy: Separate the positive root factors U_rest=∏_{β∈Φ⁺\{α}}U_β in height order. Root-string brackets show U_rest is normalized by the rank-one subgroup generated by U_{±α} and by T. Multiplication U_rest⋊(T·G_α) gives a closed algebraic subgroup: use the root-coordinate chart near 1 and the two SL₂ Bruhat charts, whose gluing includes both B and Bn_αB. Rank-one multiplication gives precisely those two double cosets. The quotient cancels U_rest and the extra torus, leaving SL₂/B₂; its U_{−α} affine chart and Weyl chart glue by z↦1/z, hence P¹. This P_α is minimal above B, not maximal parabolic. AC is inherited from root structure.

references.title: Michel Brion, Lectures on the Geometry of Flag Varieties

items.title: Fixed point for the specified Borel on a projective variety
items.statement: Assume AC. Every nonempty B-stable closed subvariety of a projective B-variety has a B-fixed point.
items.strategy: Give U a B-normal filtration by root height, with successive quotients products of Ga; refine it by T-weight lines, then append a filtration of T with Gm quotients. The in-run projective-proper theorem makes each closed projective fixed locus proper. For a Ga or Gm action on a nonempty such variety, use the in-run valuative criterion at the DVR of infinity or zero to extend the orbit map A¹ or Gm→Y to that endpoint; the unique limit is fixed by translation or scaling. Induct along the normal filtration: the fixed locus of each normal subgroup is nonempty closed and stable under the next quotient. Thus the B-fixed locus is nonempty. AC enters through B factorization and the valuative criterion.

items.title: Rational highest-weight modules from adjoint Plücker vectors
items.statement: Assume AC. For b=Lie B and p_α=Lie P_α, choose nonzero top wedges v_B∈∧^{dim b}b⊂∧^{dim b}g and v_α∈∧^{dim p_α}p_α⊂∧^{dim p_α}g; their lines generate finite-dimensional rational G-subrepresentations W_B and W_α whose differentiated modules are the irreducible highest-weight modules L(2ρ) and L(2ρ−α), with unique B-stable lines spanned by v_B and v_α.
items.strategy: The exterior adjoint representations are algebraic by the group multiplication/adjoint formulas. Explicit wedges of ordered bases choose nonzero generators of the determinant lines. B preserves each Lie subalgebra, so U fixes the determinant line; T acts on v_B by the sum of positive roots 2ρ and on v_α by 2ρ−α. Both weights are dominant (for 2ρ−α, pairing with α∨ is zero and with every other simple coroot is 2−⟨α,β∨⟩>0). In the published semisimple Lie-module decomposition, every nonzero component of such a highest vector lies in a copy of the unique L(μ); its cyclic Lie submodule is one diagonal copy, hence irreducible. Connectedness of G makes that Lie submodule G-stable, so it is a rational subrepresentation of an exterior adjoint power. The published highest-weight result supplies uniqueness of its B-stable line. This concretely integrates the only highest-weight modules needed for the two projective orbit constructions; it does not assume arbitrary Lie representations are rational. AC is required by the cited Lie classification.

items.title: Projective orbit constructions for G/B and G/Pα
items.statement: Assume AC. The orbit maps G→P(W_B), g↦g[v_B], and G→P(W_α), g↦g[v_α], have stabilizers B and P_α respectively and identify their orbits with smooth connected closed projective algebraic quotients G/B and G/P_α.
items.strategy: B and P_α fix the respective lines. If g=b n_w b′ stabilizes a highest line of weight μ, then wμ=μ. Strict dominance of 2ρ forces w=1; for μ=2ρ−α, the Weyl stabilizer is {1,s_α}, so the stabilizer is exactly B or P_α, including scheme structure by comparing Lie stabilizers. Chevalley makes each orbit image constructible in projective space; a dense constructible subset of its irreducible closure contains an open subset. Translate that open subset by G to cover the orbit, proving it locally closed. Give it the reduced locally closed structure. Its generic local ring is a field and hence regular; over C the in-run regular/smooth equivalence and openness of the smooth locus give a smooth point. G-transitivity carries this smooth point to every orbit point, so the orbit is smooth and connected. If its projective-closure boundary were nonempty, it would be a nonempty closed B-stable projective variety. The preceding fixed-point lemma gives a B-fixed line there, but each irreducible W has only its original highest line, already in the orbit. Hence the orbit is closed/projective. The big-cell sections identify the orbit with the algebraic fppf quotient functor and later give Zariski local torsor charts. AC enters via Chevalley, the Plücker representation and root lemmas.

items.title: Zariski sections of Borel and minimal-parabolic orbit maps
items.statement: Assume AC. The quotient maps G→G/B and G→G/P_α have Zariski local sections: translates of opposite-root big cells cover each quotient, and over each such chart G is the product of the root-coordinate chart with B or P_α.
items.strategy: For G/B the open U⁻B/B≅U⁻ has section u↦u. Every Bruhat cell sits in a Weyl translate of this open chart by the rank-one/Bruhat factorization, so finitely many translates cover. For G/P_α use the subgroup U⁻_{P_α} generated by negative roots outside the Levi root subsystem; its multiplication with P_α is an open immersion by the same tangent and uniqueness check, and Weyl translates cover by Bruhat. These sections explicitly trivialize the right B and P_α torsors and make associated bundles Zariski locally trivial. AC is inherited from the group construction.

references.title: Michel Brion, Lectures on the Geometry of Flag Varieties

items.title: Smooth projective semisimple flag variety
items.statement: Assume AC. For connected simply connected complex semisimple algebraic G and Borel B, the algebraic quotient G/B exists, is connected and smooth, and admits a closed projective embedding.

references.title: Michel Brion, Lectures on the Geometry of Flag Varieties

items.strategy: Use the rational highest-weight Plücker orbit G·[v_B]⊂P(W_B), whose stabilizer is B and whose boundary is empty by the Borel fixed-point argument. Smoothness follows from the smooth orbit map with B smooth, and connectedness from connected G. Zariski sections identify this closed orbit with the algebraic quotient G/B rather than only the smooth Lie quotient. AC is inherited from the Lie/root representation chain.

items.title: Bruhat cells of the flag variety
items.statement: Assume AC. For G,B,T as fixed, G/B is the disjoint union of B-orbits BwB/B indexed by W. Each cell is affine of dimension ℓ(w); the longest cell is dense open.

references.title: Michel Brion, Lectures on the Geometry of Flag Varieties

items.strategy: Pass the group-level decomposition G=⊔Bn_wB through the B torsor. On each cell cancel the stabilizer factor U∩n_wUn_w^−1 and use the root-coordinate product U_w to identify Bn_wB/B≅A^{ℓ(w)}. The longest element has ℓ(w₀)=|Φ⁺| and its cell is the dense open big cell. Explain how locally closed strata and their disjoint union are scheme-level, not just a set decomposition. AC is inherited from the root/Bruhat chain.

items.title: Borel-character equivariant line bundle
items.statement: Assume AC. For λ∈X*(T)=X*(B), let B act on C by the character −λ and define L_λ=G×^B C_{−λ} on X=G/B, with (gb,v)∼(g,b·v). The fiber at eB has B-weight −λ; this fixed sign convention gives positive degree ⟨λ,α∨⟩ on P_α/B.

references.title: Michel Brion, Lectures on the Geometry of Flag Varieties
Jacob Lurie, A Proof of the Borel–Weil–Bott Theorem
references.locator: Complete three-page note, especially Theorems 1 and 3 and Lemma 4

items.strategy: Extend λ uniquely from T across B=T⋉U by making it trivial on U. Use explicit Zariski sections of G→G/B to glue the quotient line bundle; on an overlap the transition is the B-character −λ. Verify left G-equivariance and the base-fiber weight. AC is inherited from the B/root construction.

items.title: Borel characters classify equivariant flag line bundles
items.statement: Assume AC. For the fixed simply connected semisimple G, taking the fiber over eB gives an equivalence between G-equivariant algebraic line bundles on G/B and one-dimensional algebraic B-representations; consequently their isomorphism classes are X*(B)≅X*(T).

references.title: Michel Brion, Lectures on the Geometry of Flag Varieties
Jacob Lurie, A Proof of the Borel–Weil–Bott Theorem
references.locator: Complete three-page note, especially Theorems 1 and 3 and Lemma 4

items.strategy: For a G-equivariant line bundle take its fiber at eB with the algebraic B action; conversely form G×^B of any one-dimensional B-module. Zariski sections of the B torsor yield explicit inverse bundle maps, and evaluating equivariant morphisms at eB proves full faithfulness. A character is trivial on each Ga root factor of U, so X*(B)≅X*(T). The theorem concerns equivariant line bundles only, not all Pic(G/B). AC is inherited from the group construction.

items.title: Canonical weight of a flag variety
items.statement: Assume AC. For the fixed positive roots and L_λ=G×^B C_{−λ}, the canonical line of X=G/B is ω_X≅L_{−2ρ}, with 2ρ the sum of positive roots.

references.title: Jacob Lurie, A Proof of the Borel–Weil–Bott Theorem
references.locator: Complete three-page note, especially Theorems 1 and 3 and Lemma 4

items.strategy: Differentiate the B action at eB: T_{eB}(G/B)=g/b=⊕_{β∈Φ⁺}g_{−β}, with unipotent B action triangular. The cotangent determinant therefore has B-character +∑β=2ρ. Since L_λ has base-fiber character −λ, the canonical bundle is L_{−2ρ}. Homogeneity extends the base-fiber isomorphism; AC is inherited from group/root theory.

items.title: Minimal parabolic flag projection is a projective-line bundle
items.statement: Assume AC. For a simple root α let P_α be the minimal parabolic with Weyl subgroup {1,s_α}. Then G/B→G/P_α is Zariski locally a P¹-bundle and each fiber P_α/B is P¹.

references.title: Michel Brion, Lectures on the Geometry of Flag Varieties
Jacob Lurie, A Proof of the Borel–Weil–Bott Theorem
references.locator: Complete three-page note, especially Theorems 1 and 3 and Lemma 4

items.strategy: The two projective orbit constructions give G/B and G/P_α and their map induced by B⊂P_α. The root-subgroup lemma identifies P_α/B with SL₂/B₂=P¹ via two standard affine charts. Zariski sections of G→G/P_α make the map locally (base chart)×(P_α/B), so it is a projective-line bundle. Preserve the minimal-parabolic convention and the rank-one G=P_α case. AC is inherited from group/root theory.

items.title: Flag line-bundle degree on a minimal-parabolic fiber
items.statement: Assume AC. With L_λ=G×^B C_{−λ}, its restriction to P_α/B≅P¹ has degree <λ,α∨>. In particular L_α has degree 2 and L_{−α} degree −2.

references.title: Michel Brion, Lectures on the Geometry of Flag Varieties
Jacob Lurie, A Proof of the Borel–Weil–Bott Theorem
references.locator: Complete three-page note, especially Theorems 1 and 3 and Lemma 4

items.strategy: Pull L_λ to the rank-one SL₂/B₂=P¹ chart. Restrict −λ to diag(t,t^−1): its exponent is −⟨λ,α∨⟩. The tautological O(−1) fiber at eB has exponent +1, so character exponent −m gives O(m), fixing the sign. Thus deg L_λ=⟨λ,α∨⟩, including negative m, and the root α has degree 2. AC is inherited from the rank-one/root inputs.

items.title: Relative canonical weight for a minimal-parabolic flag projection
items.statement: Assume AC. For π:G/B→G/P_α, the relative canonical line bundle is K_π=ω_{(G/B)/(G/P_α)}≅L_{−α}; its fiber degree is −2.

references.title: Jacob Lurie, A Proof of the Borel–Weil–Bott Theorem
references.locator: Complete three-page note, especially Theorems 1 and 3 and Lemma 4

items.strategy: The relative tangent at eB is p_α/b=g_{−α}, whose B-weight is −α; its dual has weight +α, hence is L_{−α} in the fixed convention. Transport equivariantly over G/B, and check its restriction to P_α/B has degree ⟨−α,α∨⟩=−2, as required for ω_{P¹}. AC is inherited from the group/root inputs.

items.title: Local normal form for a line bundle on a projective-line bundle
items.statement: Assume AC. If π:E→S is a Zariski locally trivial P¹-bundle of complex schemes and L has constant geometric fiber degree n, then after a Zariski cover of S and a chosen trivialization E_U≅P¹_U, one has L|E_U≅O_{P¹_U}(n)⊗π* M_U for a line bundle M_U on U. The line M_U is π_*(L(−n)) in that chart and the evaluation map is the stated isomorphism.
items.strategy: On an affine base chart trivializing E, set F=L⊗O(−n). Every geometric fiber F_s is O_{P¹}(0), so its cohomology is one-dimensional in degree zero and zero in degree one. The in-run bounded finite-projective universal cohomology complex has this same fiber pattern; over each base local ring split its matrices by Nakayama to obtain a rank-one locally free H⁰ and zero higher cohomology, compatible with arbitrary base change. Then M=π_*F is a line bundle. The adjunction evaluation π*M→F is an isomorphism on every geometric fiber and hence an isomorphism of line bundles by Nakayama on stalks. This proves the local normal form without assuming Pic(A[t])=Pic(A) over arbitrary bases. AC is inherited from the cohomology suppliers.

references.title: Jacob Lurie, A Proof of the Borel–Weil–Bott Theorem
references.locator: Complete three-page note, especially Theorems 1 and 3 and Lemma 4

items.title: Leray spectral sequence for sheaf cohomology
items.statement: Assume AC. For f:X→Y and an abelian sheaf F, there is a natural first-quadrant spectral sequence E₂^{p,q}=H^p(Y,R^qf_*F)⇒H^{p+q}(X,F), with the usual edge maps and finite filtration in each total degree.
items.strategy: For a continuous f:X→S and abelian sheaf F, use the published AC-qualified abelian-sheaf injective resolution to define R^qf_*F. Inverse image on abelian sheaves is exact stalkwise, so its right adjoint f_* sends abelian injectives to injectives and hence Γ(S,−)-acyclics. Apply the published Grothendieck spectral sequence to f_* then Γ(S,−), identifying Γ(S,f_*F)=Γ(X,F). To apply to O-modules use the in-run O-module injective/cohomology comparison and underlying abelian sheaf; verify the two higher-direct-image definitions agree. AC supplies injective/Cartan–Eilenberg data.

items.title: Relative projective-line cohomology and apolarity
items.statement: Assume AC. Let π:E→S be a Zariski locally trivial P¹-bundle of complex schemes, L a line bundle of constant geometric fiber degree n≥−1, and K_π=ω_{E/S}. Then R^qπ_*L=0 for q>0, R^qπ_*(L⊗K_π^{n+1})=0 for q≠1, and after fixing a nonzero invariant SL₂ apolarity normalization there is a natural isomorphism π_*L≅R¹π_*(L⊗K_π^{n+1}), compatible with base restriction and changes of trivialization.

references.title: Jacob Lurie, A Proof of the Borel–Weil–Bott Theorem
references.locator: Complete three-page note, especially Theorems 1 and 3 and Lemma 4

items.strategy: Use the preceding local normal form L=O(n)⊗π*M on each P¹_U. The in-run relative projective-space Čech calculation gives R⁰O(n)=Sym^n V^∨, R¹O(−n−2) its residue dual and all other direct images zero, also for n=−1 (both sides zero). The relative canonical is O(−2)⊗det(V)^∨ under the line convention; GL₂-equivariant apolarity Sym^n V^∨≅Sym^n V⊗det(V)^−n identifies the two terms after the K^{n+1} twist. Check the central scalar action and the M factor explicitly so the map descends under PGL₂ coordinate changes and arbitrary L transition functions. Glue and verify base restriction. AC enters through higher direct images/cohomology.

items.title: Relative projective-line cohomology shift
items.statement: Assume AC. Let π:E→S be a Zariski locally trivial P¹-bundle of complex schemes and L a line bundle of constant fiber degree n≥−1. After the fixed apolarity normalization, for every i≥0 there is a natural isomorphism H^i(E,L)≅H^{i+1}(E,L⊗K_π^{n+1}).

references.title: Jacob Lurie, A Proof of the Borel–Weil–Bott Theorem
references.locator: Complete three-page note, especially Theorems 1 and 3 and Lemma 4

items.strategy: For L, Leray has only q=0 row and identifies H^i(E,L) with H^i(S,π_*L). For L⊗K_π^{n+1}, Leray has only q=1 row and identifies H^{i+1} with H^i(S,R¹π_*(L⊗K_π^{n+1})). Apply the preceding normalized apolarity isomorphism. For n=−1 both sheaves and both sides vanish. Naturality follows from sheaf-level descent, not merely a fiberwise vector-space isomorphism. AC enters through Leray.

title: Smooth-Projective Serre Duality and Flag-Variety Line Bundles — Examples

items.title: Flag line bundles for SL₂
items.statement: Assume AC. For G=SL₂(C), B upper triangular, and T=diag(t,t⁻¹), G/B≅P¹, L_{mω₁}≅O(m), ω_{G/B}=O(−2), and the fiber degree is m.

references.title: Michel Brion, Lectures on the Geometry of Flag Varieties, §§1.2–1.4, 2.1
Jacob Lurie, A Proof of the Borel–Weil–Bott Theorem, pp. 1–3

items.strategy: Map gB to the line spanned by ge₁; compute B’s action on the tautological fiber as t and therefore L_{ω₁}=O(1) under the fixed −λ convention. Check m=−2 against the canonical bundle. AC is inherited from the named A-page suppliers.

items.title: Two minimal-parabolic projections for SL₃
items.statement: Assume AC. For G=SL₃(C), the two simple-root projections from complete flags (line L⊂plane H⊂C³) forget H or forget L, and each fiber is P¹; the corresponding fundamental line bundles have fiber-degree pairs (1,0) and (0,1).

references.title: Michel Brion, Lectures on the Geometry of Flag Varieties, §§1.2–1.4, 2.1
J. S. Milne, Algebraic Groups, Chapters 7, 21–22

items.strategy: For fixed L, planes through L form P(C³/L); for fixed H, lines in H form P(H). Restrict the two fundamental associated line bundles and compute degrees from the simple coroot pairings. AC is inherited from the named A-page suppliers.

items.title: Projective-space twist pairing in Serre duality
items.statement: Assume AC. For P²_k and d=2, the class x₀²∈H⁰(O(2)) pairs to 1 with the top Čech class x₀⁻³x₁⁻¹x₂⁻¹∈H²(O(−5)) and to 0 with the other Laurent basis classes.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Cohomology of Schemes, §§30.2, 30.8, 30.14
The Stacks Project, Duality for Schemes, §27

items.strategy: Multiply the two Laurent monomials and take the coefficient of (x₀x₁x₂)⁻¹. Check that all other degree −5 all-negative basis monomials have a different exponent vector and therefore give zero. AC is inherited from the named A-page suppliers.
